stemBlocks.value: Matrices P, Q and R have orders 2 × 3, 3 × 2 and 2 × 2 respectively. (a) State whether PQ is defined, and if so its order. (b) State whether QP is defined, and if so its order. (c) State whether PR is defined, giving a reason. (d) State the order of RP.
Think first: Write the two orders side by side: the inner numbers decide whether the product exists, and the outer numbers give its order.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p197-q08 from workbook page 197.

solutionSteps.instruction: Line up the orders for PQ.

contentBlocks.value: (2 × 3)(3 × 2): the inner numbers are 3 and 3, which match.

solutionSteps.instruction: Line up the orders for QP.

contentBlocks.value: (3 × 2)(2 × 3): the inner numbers are 2 and 2, which match.

solutionSteps.instruction: Line up the orders for PR.

contentBlocks.value: (2 × 3)(2 × 2): the inner numbers are 3 and 2, which do not match.

solutionSteps.instruction: Line up the orders for RP.

contentBlocks.value: (2 × 2)(2 × 3): the inner numbers are 2 and 2, which match.

strategyBlocks.value: For each product, line up the orders as (a × b)(c × d) and check b = c; if it holds, the product is a × d.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a) PQ is defined and has order 2 × 2  (b) QP is defined and has order 3 × 3  (c) PR is not defined, because the number of columns of P (3) does not equal the number of rows of R (2)  (d) RP has order 2 × 3

whyThisWorks.value: A product row-by-column only makes sense when each row of the first matrix has exactly as many entries as each column of the second, which is the inner-numbers rule. The surviving outer numbers become the shape of the answer. Parts (a) and (b) also show why order matters: PQ and QP are not even the same size.

commonErrors.misconception: Checking the outer numbers instead of the inner ones.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Checking the outer numbers instead of the inner ones.

commonErrors.misconception: Assuming that if PQ exists then QP must have the same order.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Assuming that if PQ exists then QP must have the same order.

commonErrors.misconception: Saying PR is defined because both matrices contain a 2.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Saying PR is defined because both matrices contain a 2.

examTip.value: Write the orders next to each other, cover the outer numbers with your fingers, and check the two inner numbers match before doing any arithmetic.
